newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil wins shipment contracts for UK oilfields.
newsitem.headline: Statoil wins shipment contracts for UK oilfields.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS (Statoil ) said on Thursday it had been commissioned to transport oil from the Durward/Dauntless and Captain fields in the U.K. sector of the North Sea.
Crude from Durward and Dauntless, operated as a single development by Amerada Hess, will be shipped to a common discharge point.
Statoil said it had chartered the shuttle tanker Aberdeen from Texaco Overseas Tankships to transport oil from the Texaco operated Captain field. The charter is for five years with options.
Under construction in Spain for delivery in December, Aberdeen has a double hull and can load up to 550,000 barrels of oil.

Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said Aberdeen could be utilised to load crude from other U.K. fields. The contract of affreightment with Texaco means that the U.S. oil company will only pay for the oil actually shipped, it said.
The new vessel brings to 18 the fleet of shuttle tankers run by the Norwegian state oil group off northwest Europe and makes Statoil the world's largest operator of such tonnage.
The latest agreements bring the number of Statoil contracts for offshore loading at British fields to six.
